key_insight: Boron doping expands the stable mixed-valence Cu-O phase window, delaying CuO formation and enabling much lower resistivity under oxygen-rich sputtering conditions.
engineering_relevance: This offers a controllable route to tune Cu-O thin-film conductivity and phase stability for transparent electrodes and photovoltaic/optoelectronic interfaces.
method: Reactive magnetron sputtering of Cu-O thin films with varying oxygen partial pressure.
Systematic boron incorporation to probe changes in phase evolution and bonding.
Characterization of phase, chemical bonding, and electrical resistivity across the processing window.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports a phase progression from Cu2O to Cu2O/Cu4O3 to CuO with increasing oxygen pressure, while highly B-doped films retained Cu4O3 under oxygen-rich conditions and reached about 0.06 Ω·cm.
watch_item: The reported benefits depend on precise oxygen partial pressure and boron incorporation control, so process reproducibility and phase purity may be challenging at scale.
paper_title: Boron-assisted stabilization of low-resistivity mixed-valence Cu-O thin films prepared by reactive magnetron sputtering
